questions.q: Why is dynamic RLS a good fit for restricting Adventure Works' regional sales managers?
options: One role with a user-mapping table filters each manager to their own territory, rather than needing a separate static role per territory
Static RLS is not supported for this kind of data at all
Dynamic RLS is required by Microsoft for any sales data
RLS cannot be applied to semantic models with more than one fact table
questions.explain: This is the exact use case Lesson 82 introduced dynamic RLS for — one role, filtering differently per signed-in manager via USERPRINCIPALNAME() and a mapping table, instead of one role per territory.

questions.q: Does the RLS role built in this lesson restrict every workspace role, or just one specific role?
options: Only the Viewer role — Admins, Members, and Contributors are unaffected by RLS regardless of role assignment
It restricts every workspace role equally
It only restricts the workspace Admin
RLS has no connection to workspace roles at all
questions.explain: This recaps Lesson 79's core rule: RLS only ever restricts Viewers. Anyone with edit permission (Admin, Member, Contributor) bypasses RLS entirely.

questions.q: What should be checked before assigning real people to the new RLS role?
options: Validate the filter with Test as role first, and confirm the user-mapping table's email format matches what USERPRINCIPALNAME() actually returns in the service
Nothing — real people can be assigned immediately with no validation
Only that the role has a name
Only that the semantic model has been refreshed once
questions.explain: This directly reuses Lesson 82's guidance: validate with Test as role, and double-check the UPN/email format match before trusting the filter with real users.

questions.q: What refresh frequency does this lesson recommend for the capstone's sales dashboard, and why?
options: A daily refresh — realistic for a dashboard nobody needs updated minute-by-minute
Every 5 minutes, for maximum freshness regardless of need
Refresh should be disabled entirely for this project
Hourly refresh, to match dashboard tile refresh behavior exactly
questions.explain: The scope never called for real-time data (Lesson 85 already made that call for Import mode), so a nightly scheduled refresh is a proportionate choice here.

questions.q: What access level does the app audience get in this lesson, and why?
options: View access only, since Lesson 84's scope never called for anyone outside leadership to edit or rebuild the dashboard
Full Contributor access for every audience member
Admin access, so they can modify the underlying semantic model
No access at all — the app is left unpublished
questions.explain: Matching access to the original scope matters: since the project was never meant to let the VP or managers edit the dashboard, view-only access is the correct, scope-consistent choice.
